pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.7 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum Deus sit infinitus?
pairs.answer: Cum igitur esse divinum non sit esse receptum in aliquo, sed ipse sit suum esse subsistens, ut supra ostensum est; manifestum est quod ipse Deus sit infinitus et perfectus.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article's interrogative title (Utrum Deus sit infinitus), normalized with a question mark. The Respondeo opens with a long historical preamble about the antiqui philosophi and the distinction of materia/forma (Respondeo dicendum quod omnes antiqui philosophi... habet rationem perfecti), which does not answer; it then has a setup sentence (Illud autem quod est maxime formale... est ipsum esse). The answer's start is advanced to the operative answering sentence beginning 'Cum igitur esse divinum...' and ends at the first full stop after 'infinitus et perfectus'. What follows the cut is the formulaic 'Et per hoc patet responsio ad primum.' and the replies to objections.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.7 a.2
pairs.question: Utrum aliquid aliud quam Deus possit esse infinitum per essentiam?
pairs.answer: Aliquid praeter Deum potest esse infinitum secundum quid, sed non simpliciter.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article's interrogative title, normalized with a question mark. The answer is the first sentence of the Respondeo (after stripping the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod' and capitalizing 'aliquid'), which directly and completely answers the whether-question (yes secundum quid, no simpliciter). The cut is at the first full stop; what follows is the elaboration distinguishing infinitum of matter vs. form ('Si enim loquamur de infinito...').

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.7 a.4
pairs.question: Utrum possit esse infinitum in rebus secundum multitudinem?
pairs.answer: Impossibile est esse multitudinem infinitam actu, sive per se, sive per accidens.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article's interrogative title, normalized with a question mark. The Respondeo opens with a long doxographical preamble reporting the opinion of Avicenna and Algazel (Respondeo dicendum quod circa hoc fuit duplex opinio... multitudinem infinitam per accidens), which does not state Aquinas's own answer; then 'Sed hoc est impossibile' introduces the refutation. The answer's start is advanced past the refutation's argument (Quia omnem multitudinem oportet esse... non enim in vanum agens aliquod operatur... sub certo numero) to the clean operative conclusion 'Unde impossibile est...', with the framing connective 'Unde' dropped and 'impossibile' capitalized; it ends at the full stop. What follows the cut is 'Sed esse multitudinem infinitam in potentia, possibile est...' (the in-potentia qualification) and the replies to objections.
